Applies to: Morphology: elastomer; Modifier / filler: Unfilled / unspecified
Basis: A thermoplastic elastomer is soft because its chains are held only at their hard blocks. The Cambridge Materials Data Book's table of Young's modulus (II.3, p. 11 of the book, PDF p. 13; Granta Design's data) prints every elastomer class it lists between 0.0007 and 0.04 GPa: polyurethane elastomers (elPU) 0.002-0.003 GPa, EVA 0.01-0.04, silicone elastomers 0.005-0.02. Its rigid thermoplastic polyurethanes (tpPU, 1.31-2.07 GPa) are not elastomers and not this kind: a rubbery TPU filament is sold by its Shore A or soft Shore D hardness. The limit is set well above the book's elastomers, at the experts' 0.5 GPa (C32, V26; Shore 95A is about 0.04 GPa), because the hardest unfilled elastomer filaments here, Shore D TPUs, publish 0.39 to 0.40 GPa; the kind's own published maximum widens it further where a product prints more, and the engine's 10 % scatter is added before it fails anything.

Reason words: An unfilled product of its polymer
Basis: Without a filler, a filament's density is its polymer's: unfilled PLA cannot exceed 1,330 kg/m³ (C32, V26). The range is the neat range polymers.csv records for the material's polymer, read only where that row names a registered source, and widened to the kind's own published extremes among its products that are not variants. It stays reported until the polymers' neat densities have registered sources (stage 2c of the screening build).
